# Work & Research

November 2026

## Agent engineering

<section id="nova-agent">

### Nova Agent

*Production agents · Insurance*

When we started on placement, we wrote each step into a workflow and connected the steps in code. As the models got better at choosing tools, we could let operators teach Nova a procedure as a Skill. The model decides when that procedure fits the task.

One placement task can involve more than 50 PDFs. My work includes making policy and submission documents available to Nova and connecting it to the internal tools operators use. We sit down with operators to review what it produces, including draft contracts and emails. Their feedback shapes both the tools and the Skills.

</section>

<section id="nori">

### Nori

*Organization assistant · In development*

Nori delegates research and coding tasks for Rein. In one test, we restarted Nori with two tasks underway. It found both tasks, followed up on missing results, and delivered a summary in Slack.

I'm working on what happens when someone changes a request while a worker is still running. If the original result arrives late, Nori needs to associate it with the old request.

[Nori project overview](/?page=Projects/Project#nori)

</section>

## Organization building

<section id="rein-foundation">

### Rein Protocol Foundation

*AI agent safety · Community and open-source work*

We incorporated Rein in Wyoming in October 2026 to support open-source work and public education on AI agent safety. I worked on setting up the Foundation and building its website. Visitors can browse free learning materials, suggest a resource, or apply to help organize a project.

We are also trying out agents in our own operations. Nori can help prepare work for review. People at Rein decide what to take on and who can authorize an action.

[Visit Rein Protocol Foundation](https://rein-protocol.org/)

## Research in progress

<section id="agent-safety">

### Agent permissions and safety

*SystemOne / S1-P · Research in progress*

I study whether a model can judge which tool calls an agent has permission to make. In AgentDojo, I record the decisions throughout a task. This lets me see both when a simulated user approved a conflicting transfer and when it refused a read the agent needed.

In a small development run, we repeated the same three tasks across eight methods after changing the evaluation harness. Under attack, successful attacks fell from six runs to three out of 24. Completed user tasks also fell, from nine runs to two. I am investigating why the simulated user refused necessary reads.

</section>

## Selected research

<section id="fineedit">

### FineEdit

*Findings of EMNLP 2025*

Instruction-driven edits must preserve surrounding content and respect the structure of code, LaTeX, and database languages.

Co-authored FineEdit, connecting a specialized editing model with the InstrEditBench benchmark for targeted modifications.

The research evaluates precise edits across structured domains and extends evaluation to multi-turn editing scenarios.

[Read the paper](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.118/)

</section>

<section id="treediff">

### TreeDiff

*SURGeLLM at ACL 2026*

Random token masking in diffusion language models does not capture the syntactic boundaries and hierarchical dependencies of code.

Co-authored TreeDiff, a syntax-aware diffusion framework that uses abstract syntax tree structure in the corruption process.

The method masks tokens belonging to selected AST nodes, aligning reconstruction with program structure. Published in the SURGeLLM workshop proceedings at ACL 2026.

[Read the paper](https://aclanthology.org/2026.surgellm-1.5/)

</section>

<section id="infant-agent">

### Infant Agent

*Agent research · arXiv preprint, 2024*

Multi-step engineering and reasoning tasks need coordination beyond a single model response.

Co-authored research on a tool-integrated, logic-driven agent architecture with task-aware functions and hierarchical management.

The work studies memory retrieval, tool integration, and API costs, with evaluations on software engineering and mathematical reasoning tasks.

[Read the paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.01114)

</section>
